title: control-plane: add residency policy schema + validation + admin endpoints (with migrations)
author: Benji Okafor
description: Summary: Introduces first-class residency policies in the control plane, including schema + persistence, validation rules, admin CRUD endpoints, and a migration path for existing orgs/projects. This is the foundational layer used by routing/gateway enforcement (separate PRs) and by Console settings UX. Key points: (1) New entity: ResidencyPolicy with scope=org|project|api_key, allowed_regions[] + primary_region, and explicit fallback controls. (2) Validation: deterministic, fail-closed on invalid configs; prevents primary_region not in allowed set; blocks ambiguous overlaps at same scope; enforces precedence rules (api_key > project > org) while allowing inherit semantics. (3) Admin API: internal-only endpoints behind RBAC permission control_plane.residency_policy:read|write; supports list/get/create/update/delete and dry-run validate. (4) Migration: seeds default “inherit/unrestricted” policies for existing orgs (no behavior change) and adds nullable columns/tables behind a feature flag for staged rollout. (5) Tests: unit tests for validation matrix + precedence + migration; API contract tests for admin endpoints. Notes: This PR intentionally does NOT change routing behavior; it only provides config + decision inputs for downstream enforcement.
commits: control-plane: add residency_policy tables + ORM models
control-plane: add admin endpoints + RBAC wiring
migrations: seed default org policy (inherit/unrestricted) behind flag
tests: validation matrix + migration coverage + API contract tests
docs: add internal API notes + example payloads
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can we clarify default behavior for existing orgs? We must ensure no routing changes prior to enforcement rollout. If we “seed” policies, make sure they resolve to unrestricted/inherit, not implicitly pinned to a primary region. Also, prefer that absence of policy evaluates as “allow all” (for now) and is distinguishable from a user-configured allowlist. Benji Okafor (author): Agree. I updated the model to support mode=INHERIT|EXPLICIT and made the migration create an INHERIT org policy only when the feature flag residency_policy_service.seed_defaults is enabled in that environment. Additionally, resolver now returns a DecisionSource (none|inherit|explicit) so downstream can enforce stricter behavior later without guessing. Jordan Lee (review): Precedence rules look right, but I’m worried about overlapping EXPLICIT policies at the same scope (e.g., two project policies). Do we enforce uniqueness? Benji Okafor: Yes. Added unique constraint (scope, scope_id) + validation to fail with 409 conflict on create. Marcus Lin (review): For admin endpoints, ensure we’re not returning raw internal IDs that could be mistaken as stable external identifiers. Also log audit events in a follow-up? Benji Okafor: Kept policy_id as a UUID returned only on admin APIs (internal). Public API is separate and will not expose policy_id in the initial cut (per Naomi’s guidance). I added structured server logs on create/update/delete for now; full audit log events tracked in ENG-4840. Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): api_key scope: confirm scope_id maps to our internal key ID and not the secret prefix. Also ensure no accidental acceptance of user-provided API key strings. Benji Okafor: Correct—scope_id must be the internal key UUID; routes reject non-UUIDs. Added tests for this and updated the route docs. Michael Nguyen (review): Migration safety: do not require backfill to succeed for deploy. These migrations should be additive, with indexes created concurrently where possible. Benji Okafor: Updated migrations to be additive; indexes created with CONCURRENTLY where supported; seeding migration is gated and can be skipped safely. Chloe Martin (review): Please include a dry-run validation endpoint for Console to show errors without saving. Benji Okafor: Added POST /admin/residency_policies/validate returning normalized policy + validation errors/warnings; used by Console draft UX. Final: Approvals by Ethan, Jordan, Marcus after last push. CI green after rerun of contract tests (flake due to local port collision in runner).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Ethan Park. Squash commit: 9f3c2c0 control-plane: residency policy schema + validation + admin API.
release_notes: Internal-only: Control plane now supports residency policy objects (org/project/api_key) with validation and admin CRUD endpoints. No customer-facing behavior change without routing/gateway enforcement.
